scope: Independent read-only review, limited host helpers and one red/green recorder CLI regression using fake QEMU/capture. No real Cargo/GDB/VM/fullsuite run by this reviewer.
identified_issue: Coverage symbols were copied after the QEMU version probe although kernel/BIOS/initrd were already copied.
initial_counterexample: initial-mixed-freeze-receipt.json uses valid replacement EM62 and demonstrates controller timing split; not an actual guest/symbol mismatch acceptance claim.
red_green_regression: version-case-replay.json preserves original raw statuses. Old bc recorder fails the new regression; reordered 67f passes with old symbol copy retained. The final alias revision changes only snapshot_arguments, leaving the tested main and every other function byte-identical.
read_only_conclusions: Actual QEMU kernel/initrd/BIOS arguments and actual capture symbol argument point to exclusive private copies.
The second ordinary-recorder source read must match selection source SHA/size/path before exact-byte compile; a changed source was rejected.
capture_artifact checks a stable regular file descriptor, named identity and stat before/after reads; destination uses exclusive creation.
Copy data/identity/stat changes fail before or after QEMU, while changes to original mutable build outputs are allowed after capture.
Post-finalization copy failure records wrapper125/error and is rejected by downstream coverage_binding; finalized sidecar alone cannot make that record pass.
The final alias parser preserves canonical artifact metadata keys, recognizes supported double-hyphen flags and skips known valued options including literal -append values.
Optional initrd, original UNIX transport, explicit local TCP/capture strategy and existing coverage checks remain in effect.
limitations: No atomic multi-file build snapshot or protection against arbitrary privileged writers is claimed.
Private copies are retained in live output. archive.py filters binary suffixes, and root plans explicit stable-FD artifact preservation/deduplication/chunks for final public evidence.
Producer-owned fullsuite and full22 real integration results are separate from these reviewer fixtures.
decision: No remaining blocking issue found in the final measured candidate.
